_note: Cited public values and forms for aerodynamics; our own numbers are computed, never typed. See SOURCES.md.

induced_drag_coefficient.source: NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics, 'Induced Drag Coefficient' (T. Benson)
induced_drag_coefficient.what: induced drag coefficient; e = 1.0 for an elliptic distribution; AR = span^2 / wing area

induced_drag_force.form: D_i = L^2 / (1/2 rho V^2 pi b^2), b the wingspan
induced_drag_force.what: induced drag of a wing in terms of its lift and span (span efficiency 1)

induced_share_wide_body_cruise.what: induced drag as a fraction of the total drag of a typical twin-engine wide-body aircraft at cruise ('approximately 37 %'; skin friction 'almost 48 %') - evidence for trap T9, not a test of our code

joukowsky_kutta_circulation.form: Gamma = 4 pi V_inf R sin(alpha + asin(mu_y / R)), R = sqrt((1 - mu_x)^2 + mu_y^2), for z = zeta + 1/zeta and a circle centred at mu = mu_x + i mu_y through zeta = 1
joukowsky_kutta_circulation.what: circulation fixed by the Kutta condition on a Joukowsky airfoil

thin_airfoil_centre_of_pressure_symmetri.what: centre of pressure of a thin symmetric airfoil, as a fraction of the chord behind the leading edge ('exactly one quarter of the chord behind the leading edge')

thin_airfoil_lift_slope.form: c_l = 2 pi alpha (thin symmetric airfoil, alpha in radians); c_l = c_l0 + 2 pi alpha (cambered)
thin_airfoil_lift_slope.how_obtained: read on the page (secondary source; the page cites Abbott & von Doenhoff and Clancy, not read)
thin_airfoil_lift_slope.what: section lift-curve slope per radian of a thin airfoil of infinite span

wagner_garrick_fit.how_obtained: read first-hand in the extracted PDF text
wagner_garrick_fit.source: Dawson & Brunton, arXiv:2104.15122v2, Eq. (2); absolute error '2%' (text under Fig. 2)
wagner_garrick_fit.what: I. E. Garrick's algebraic approximation of Wagner's function, same non-dimensional time

wagner_jones_fit.form: phi(s) = 1 - C1 exp(-eps1 s) - C2 exp(-eps2 s), s = U t / (semi-chord)
wagner_jones_fit.how_obtained: both read first-hand (the arXiv PDF text was extracted and searched; the BYU page was fetched). The primary report (R. T. Jones, NACA TN 667, 1938, as cited by Dawson & Brunton) was not read
wagner_jones_fit.second_source: BYU FLOW Lab, Aeroelasticity.jl documentation, 'Wagner's Function' (C1 = 0.165, C2 = 0.335, eps1 = 0.0455, eps2 = 0.3; exponent (u/b) t with b the semi-chord)
wagner_jones_fit.source: S. T. M. Dawson & S. L. Brunton, 'Improved approximations to the Wagner function using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics', arXiv:2104.15122v2 (2021), Eq. (1) and Table 1; the absolute error of the fit is 'less than 1%' (text under Fig. 2)
wagner_jones_fit.what: R. T. Jones' two-exponential approximation of Wagner's function (growth of circulatory lift after a step in incidence); time made non-dimensional with the semi-chord and the free-stream speed
